title: Flood exposure and weak urban coordination can turn location advantage into spatial underperformance
source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11444, Evaluating Spatial Underperformance: A Spatial Computable General Equilibrium Model Applied to Ho Chi Minh City, September 2026
geography: Greater Ho Chi Minh City metropolitan area, 116 spatial cells across Ho Chi Minh City and neighboring provinces; Thu Duc households, firms, commuters, land markets, and flood-exposed communities

denominator.unit: spatial cells in the Greater Ho Chi Minh City metropolitan model

thu_duc_productivity.value: Thu Duc's calibrated productivity is roughly one-third of the metropolitan average

frontier_gap.value: frontier output is more than five times the business-as-usual level in the model

flood_channel.value: the model evaluates flood risk as a determinant of productivity and residential amenity alongside transport and land use

observations.method: Spatial computable general equilibrium model with endogenous firm location, household residence and commuting, land-use intensity, agglomeration externalities, and cell-level productivity and amenity calibration.
observations.uncertainty: Calibrated productivity and frontier comparisons are model-based and depend on spatial equilibrium, flood, transport, land-use, and agglomeration assumptions; they are not observed causal output gaps.
observations.subgroup: Flood-exposed households, commuters, firms, renters and landowners, workers choosing residence and jobs, and neighborhoods with different access to transport and amenities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Apparent underperformance may reflect measurement, transitional urbanization, land-market constraints, or institutional fragmentation rather than flood exposure alone.

denominator.unit: spatial cells in the Greater Ho Chi Minh City model

flood_mitigation.value: flood mitigation raises sectoral total factor productivity by 12% to 21% and residential amenity by 10% to 13% in the model

employment_base.value: flood mitigation broadens the sectoral employment base more than the other interventions examined

intervention_set.value: the model compares innovation zones, flood mitigation, transport, and a cumulative package

observations.method: Counterfactual spatial general-equilibrium scenarios through 2040, with endogenous responses in firms, households, commuting, land use, and agglomeration.
observations.uncertainty: Scenario effects are conditional on model structure and implementation; they do not estimate construction costs, distributional incidence, displacement, or realized adaptation quality.
observations.subgroup: Workers and firms in exposed cells, residents choosing homes, commuters using transport networks, low-income households, and sectors with different location and flood sensitivity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Flood protection can raise amenity and productivity but may increase land values, displacement, or unequal access if housing and land governance do not distribute the gains.

observations.period: 2026-2040; metropolitan redistribution versus net new growth

denominator.unit: Greater Ho Chi Minh City metropolitan model cells

cumulative_package.value: innovation zones, flood mitigation, and transport reach about 31% of the modeled frontier

output_change.value: the cumulative package raises output roughly two-thirds above business as usual

net_new_share.value: about 56% of the package's output gain is net new metropolitan output rather than activity reallocated from elsewhere

observations.method: Metropolitan spatial equilibrium simulation distinguishing net new output from activity reallocated across locations.
observations.uncertainty: The modeled net-new share depends on assumptions about agglomeration, land, commuting, firm mobility, and other regions; it is not a realized regional multiplier.
observations.subgroup: Residents and firms in Thu Duc and neighboring cells, commuters, municipal governments, landowners, renters, and communities facing flood or displacement risk.
observations.counterinterpretation: A package that benefits the metropolitan economy can still create local losers or unequal access; aggregate net-new output does not guarantee equitable household welfare.

boundary: This record adds a place-and-climate route linking flood exposure, productivity, amenity, transport, land use, commuting, agglomeration, and metropolitan redistribution. It is a spatial general-equilibrium simulation, not a causal estimate of completed infrastructure, and does not establish equitable household welfare, displacement outcomes, or realized net-new growth.
